Two record weaknesses give this case a foothold: the Britannica source is published 2026-10-08, after the as-of date, so it must be excluded from an as-of-2026-10-01 judgment; and the company's own release uses conditional language ('The Board also intends to appoint D'Amaro as a director...'), showing parts of the transition were still contingent at announcement. Stripping the future-dated Britannica item, corroboration rests on the company press release plus NPR/PBS/Variety, all from a single day, with no primary regulatory filing (8-K) in the record confirming the CEO change actually closed on March 18, 2026. If an 8-K or later reporting showed a reversal, delayed handover, or D'Amaro's departure, FALSE would be the correct verdict. That said, the 2026-09-29 CNBC piece states D'Amaro 'stepped in as CEO at Disney in March, replacing longtime chief executive Bob Iger,' which makes the FALSE case thin on the current record.
